1: /**
2:  * Pause media while dictating: pause what is playing when a recording starts, play the
3:  * same sessions again when it ends.
4:  *
5:  * Pure policy with injected effects, so every end reason and the back-to-back case are
6:  * tested without a desktop. The effects are the only place that knows about Windows.
7:  *
8:  * Rules:
9:  *  - Only sessions that were Playing are paused, and only those are remembered.
10:  *  - A resume plays just those sessions, and the effect skips any that is no longer Paused
11:  *    (the person already pressed play, or closed it). Nothing is ever started that was not
12:  *    playing before the dictation.
13:  *  - Effects run one at a time, in the order they were asked, and each checks at the moment
14:  *    it runs whether a recording is on. A dictation that starts while a resume is waiting
15:  *    therefore keeps the media paused, and never pauses it twice.
16:  *  - `recordingStarted` and `recordingEnded` return at once. Nothing here can delay a
17:  *    recording or surface as a dictation error: failures go to `log` and stop there.
18:  */
19: 
20: export interface MediaEffects {
21:   /** Pause every session that is Playing and return the ids of the ones it paused. */
22:   pausePlaying(): Promise<string[]>;
23:   /** Play each of these sessions that is still Paused. */
24:   resume(ids: string[]): Promise<void>;
25: }
26: 
27: export interface MediaPauseDeps {
28:   effects: MediaEffects;
29:   /** The `pauseMediaWhileDictating` setting, read when a recording starts. */
30:   enabled: () => boolean;
31:   /** Receives lines like `could not pause: <reason>`; the caller files them under "media". */
32:   log: (message: string) => void;
33: }
34: 
35: export class MediaPausePolicy {
36:   /** Sessions this policy paused and has not yet played again. */
37:   private readonly held = new Set<string>();
38:   private recording = false;
39:   private closed = false;
40:   /** Effects run through this chain, so they never overlap and keep their order. */
41:   private chain: Promise<void> = Promise.resolve();
42: 
43:   constructor(private readonly deps: MediaPauseDeps) {}
44: 
45:   /** A recording is starting (or has just been asked to). */
46:   recordingStarted(): void {
47:     if (this.closed) return;
48:     this.recording = true;
49:     this.enqueue(async () => {
50:       // Ended or cancelled before this got its turn: pause nothing.
51:       if (!this.recording || this.closed) return;
52:       let on: boolean;
53:       try {
54:         on = this.deps.enabled();
55:       } catch (error) {
56:         this.fail('could not read the setting', error);
57:         return;
58:       }
59:       if (!on) return;
60:       try {
61:         for (const id of await this.deps.effects.pausePlaying()) this.held.add(id);
62:       } catch (error) {
63:         this.fail('could not pause', error);
64:       }
65:     });
66:   }
67: 
68:   /** The recording is over, for any reason. Safe to call more than once. */
69:   recordingEnded(): void {
70:     this.recording = false;
71:     this.enqueue(() => this.resumeHeld());
72:   }
73: 
74:   /** Quit: play what is paused, and ignore everything after. Resolves when that is done. */
75:   async shutdown(): Promise<void> {
76:     this.recording = false;
77:     this.enqueue(() => this.resumeHeld());
78:     await this.settled();
79:     this.closed = true;
80:   }
81: 
82:   /** Resolves once every effect asked for so far has finished. */
83:   async settled(): Promise<void> {
84:     let seen: Promise<void>;
85:     do {
86:       seen = this.chain;
87:       await seen;
88:     } while (seen !== this.chain);
89:   }
90: 
91:   private async resumeHeld(): Promise<void> {
92:     // A new dictation began while this waited: the media stays paused for it.
93:     if (this.recording || this.held.size === 0) return;
94:     const ids = [...this.held];
95:     this.held.clear();
96:     try {
97:       await this.deps.effects.resume(ids);
98:     } catch (error) {
99:       // Not retried: a session that will not play is the person's to press.
100:       this.fail('could not resume', error);
101:     }
102:   }
103: 
104:   private enqueue(work: () => Promise<void>): void {
105:     this.chain = this.chain.then(work).catch((error: unknown) => this.fail('unexpected failure', error));
106:   }
107: 
108:   private fail(what: string, error: unknown): void {
109:     try {
110:       this.deps.log(`${what}: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`);
111:     } catch {
112:       // The log itself must never be the reason a dictation fails.
113:     }
114:   }
115: }

1: /**
2:  * The PowerShell behind "Pause media while dictating".
3:  *
4:  * Windows lists every app that is playing media (Spotify, a YouTube tab in Edge or Chrome,
5:  * a podcast app) as a session of the Global System Media Transport Controls. The scripts
6:  * below ask that list which sessions are Playing, pause those, and later play the same ones
7:  * again if each is still Paused.
8:  *   https://learn.microsoft.com/uwp/api/windows.media.control.globalsystemmediatransportcontrolssessionmanager
9:  *
10:  * They run in Windows PowerShell 5.1, which can load the WinRT type by name but cannot
11:  * `await` an `IAsyncOperation`; the documented reflection route is `AsTask` from
12:  * `System.WindowsRuntimeSystemExtensions`, called once per result type.
13:  *
14:  * Nothing here imports Electron, so the builders and the parser are tested on any platform.
15:  * Ids reach a script only as base64, never as text: a session id is chosen by whatever app
16:  * is playing, so it is untrusted.
17:  */
18: 
19: /** Long enough for any real list; a script is never built from more than this. */
20: const MAX_IDS = 64;
21: const MAX_ID_LENGTH = 512;
22: 
23: /**
24:  * Defines `Invoke-UvAwait` and `Get-UvMediaSessions`. The media host runs it once at start;
25:  * a one-shot process runs it in front of the body. No backtick may appear (these are
26:  * template literals), so the generic name `IAsyncOperation`1` is built from [char]96.
27:  */
28: export const MEDIA_PRELUDE = `
29: $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
30: Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Runtime.WindowsRuntime
31: $null = [Windows.Media.Control.GlobalSystemMediaTransportControlsSessionManager,Windows.Media.Control,ContentType=WindowsRuntime]
32: $uvAsyncName = 'IAsyncOperation' + [char]96 + '1'
33: $uvAsTask = @([System.WindowsRuntimeSystemExtensions].GetMethods() | Where-Object { $_.Name -eq 'AsTask' -and $_.GetParameters().Count -eq 1 -and $_.GetParameters()[0].ParameterType.Name -eq $uvAsyncName })[0]
34: function Invoke-UvAwait($operation, [Type]$resultType) {
35:   $task = $uvAsTask.MakeGenericMethod($resultType).Invoke($null, @($operation))
36:   if (-not $task.Wait(3000)) { throw 'a media request timed out' }
37:   return $task.Result
38: }
39: function Get-UvMediaSessions {
40:   $managerType = [Windows.Media.Control.GlobalSystemMediaTransportControlsSessionManager]
41:   $manager = Invoke-UvAwait ($managerType::RequestAsync()) $managerType
42:   return @($manager.GetSessions())
43: }
44: function ConvertTo-UvId([string]$text) { return [Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString([Convert]::FromBase64String($text)) }
45: `;
46: 
47: const OWN_ID = /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$/;
48: 
49: /**
50:  * Pause every session that is Playing and print `UVPAUSED:<base64 id>` for each one that
51:  * accepted. The app's own sessions are skipped (`ownAppId`), and a session that throws is
52:  * skipped without stopping the rest.
53:  */
54: export function pausePlayingScript(ownAppId = 'ai.useful.voice'): string {
55:   if (!OWN_ID.test(ownAppId)) throw new Error('the app id has characters a script may not carry');
56:   return `
57: $uvOwn = '${ownAppId}'
58: foreach ($s in @(Get-UvMediaSessions)) {
59:   try {
60:     $id = [string]$s.SourceAppUserModelId
61:     if ($id -eq $uvOwn) { continue }
62:     if ($s.GetPlaybackInfo().PlaybackStatus.ToString() -ne 'Playing') { continue }
63:     if (Invoke-UvAwait ($s.TryPauseAsync()) ([bool])) {
64:       Write-Output ('UVPAUSED:' + [Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($id)))
65:     }
66:   } catch { Write-Output 'UVSKIP:session' }
67: }
68: `;
69: }
70: 
71: /** The ids as `base64,base64,...`: the only form in which they enter a script. */
72: export function encodeSessionIds(ids: string[]): string {
73:   if (ids.length === 0 || ids.length > MAX_IDS) throw new Error('a resume needs between 1 and 64 session ids');
74:   return ids
75:     .map((id) => {
76:       if (id.length === 0 || id.length > MAX_ID_LENGTH) throw new Error('a session id is empty or too long');
77:       return Buffer.from(id, 'utf8').toString('base64');
78:     })
79:     .join(',');
80: }
81: 
82: /**
83:  * Play each listed session that is still Paused and print `UVRESUMED:<n>`. A session the
84:  * person already played, stopped or closed is left alone.
85:  */
86: export function resumeScript(ids: string[]): string {
87:   const encoded = encodeSessionIds(ids);
88:   // base64 and commas only: nothing in `encoded` can end the quote it sits in.
89:   if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9+/=,]+$/.test(encoded)) throw new Error('the encoded ids have unexpected characters');
90:   return `
91: $uvWanted = @('${encoded}'.Split(',') | ForEach-Object { ConvertTo-UvId $_ })
92: $uvResumed = 0
93: foreach ($s in @(Get-UvMediaSessions)) {
94:   try {
95:     $id = [string]$s.SourceAppUserModelId
96:     if ($uvWanted -notcontains $id) { continue }
97:     if ($s.GetPlaybackInfo().PlaybackStatus.ToString() -ne 'Paused') { continue }
98:     if (Invoke-UvAwait ($s.TryPlayAsync()) ([bool])) { $uvResumed++ }
99:   } catch { Write-Output 'UVSKIP:session' }
100: }
101: Write-Output ('UVRESUMED:' + $uvResumed)
102: `;
103: }
104: 
105: /** The ids `pausePlayingScript` reports, from its output. Anything else in the output is ignored. */
106: export function parsePausedOutput(stdout: string): string[] {
107:   const ids = new Set<string>();
108:   for (const raw of stdout.split(/\r?\n/)) {
109:     const match = /^UVPAUSED:([A-Za-z0-9+/]+={0,2})$/.exec(raw.trim());
110:     if (!match) continue;
111:     const id = Buffer.from(match[1] as string, 'base64').toString('utf8');
112:     if (id.length > 0 && id.length <= MAX_ID_LENGTH) ids.add(id);
113:   }
114:   return [...ids];
115: }

- **Resume waiting for transcription**: `recordingEvent('end')` fires in `stopRecording` before `run(session, process)`, and in `cancel`/`recorderFailed`/the start failure before any transcription.
- **Resuming media the user had already paused**: only sessions that accepted the pause are remembered, and the resume script re-checks `Paused`.
- **Our own sound cues being paused**: cues play through `Media.SoundPlayer` in the delivery host (winmm), not a GSMTC session; the `ai.useful.voice` skip is extra safety.
- **Startup settings or an old settings file flipping the feature on wrongly**: `normaliseSettings` keeps only real booleans and defaults to on for a missing key.
- **Unhandled rejection from `warm()` or quit**: `PowerShellHost.start()` never rejects, `enqueue` catches every failure, and the shutdown chain never rejects.
- **A stuck media queue**: each host request has a timeout, a dead host is restarted and then given up on with one-shot fallback, and `dispose` rejects pending requests.
- **The media host leaking past quit**: `dispose()` kills it and nulls the module singleton.
- **`FakeMedia`/`setMedia` reaching users**: the hooks are installed only under `--e2e`.
- **Quit blocking on a slow player**: the 2.5 s race bounds it (only the cleared-`held` consequence is reported above).
